origin.description: A short description of a table-like object. The first element should carry the dimensions and the data source. Further elements can carry extra facts, such as grouping.
origin.details: The default method forwards to obj_sum. The name of that element is Description. A data.frame is not a tbl, so data.frame(a = 1) uses this default and the value is the object summary, not the dimensions alone. The tbl method, which names the line "A data frame" and stores dim_desc, applies only to an object of class tbl. Building the named vector with c() drops the short attribute, so the print shows the name and the text.
origin.value: A named character vector. The first element describes the dimensions, and its name describes the source.
origin.example:
tbl_sum(1:10)
tbl_sum(matrix(1:10))
tbl_sum(data.frame(a = 1))
tbl_sum(Sys.Date())
tbl_sum(Sys.time())
tbl_sum(mean)

translation.description: The default named pair. The name is Description and the value is obj_sum. A DataFrame is not a tbl, so it uses that default.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The same objects as obj_sum. A DataFrame is summarised with obj_sum, not with the dimensions alone.

translation.details: The return value is a string subclass. The text is obj_sum and the name attribute is Description. The short attribute is not copied. data.frame(a = 1) is therefore "df [1 × 1]", not "1 × 1". The example prints the name and then the text.
translation.value: A string with a name attribute.
translation.example:
from datetime import date, datetime

from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.unicode": True})

from pillar._vec import DataFrame, Matrix
from pillar.summary import tbl_sum


def mean(values):
    return values


def show(value):
    print(value.name)
    print(value)


show(tbl_sum(list(range(1, 11))))
show(tbl_sum(Matrix(list(range(1, 11)), 10)))
show(tbl_sum(DataFrame({"a": [1]})))
show(tbl_sum(date.today()))
show(tbl_sum(datetime.now()))
show(tbl_sum(mean))
